The flintlock was invented in the early 17th century and quickly became a substitute for earlier ignition firearms such as the snaplock, matchlock, and wheel-lock. Over the following two centuries, the flintlock was widely used before being replaced by the percussion cap, and eventually by cartridge-based rifles in the mid-19th century. Despite being far inferior to modern firearms, flintlocks remain popular among black powder enthusiasts.

Both the French Revolution and the Napoleonic era pursued an innovative military doctrine. The influence of this period persisted even through the American Civil War and the early stages of World War I. Cheap and small weapons with hastily trained soldiers allowed armies to expand to unprecedented sizes, leading to the division of armies into divisions, and later into corps. Artillery divisions also emerged during this period.

Muzzle-loaded rifles are firearms that load projectiles and powder through the muzzle. Hand-held rifles were fully developed in the 1740s. The typical image of a muzzle-loaded rifle is the Kentucky rifle, although it was actually invented in Pennsylvania. The American long rifle evolved from the German hunting rifle.

Breech-loaded rifles are weapons with a space at the end of the barrel or bore for loading shells or bullets. Although breech-loaded weapons appeared as early as the 14th century, they did not become successful until the 19th century due to advances in precision engineering and mechanical engineering.

Bolt-action refers to rifles that require manual operation to feed a cartridge into the chamber (loading) and to extract the spent case from the chamber (unloading). The first bolt-action rifle was created by Johann von der Luis in 1824 while developing breech-loaded weapons. Over the following half-century, bolt-action designs underwent continuous development in Europe and reached their peak during World War I: various bolt-action designs could be seen on the weapons of every army on the battlefield.

The Gatling gun was patented by Richard Gatling in 1861 and was the first auto-loading weapon capable of providing controlled, sustained fire. It made a brief appearance during the American Civil War, and was further developed and used in the Franco-Prussian War and the Northwest Rebellion. Many armies purchased Gatling guns in the 19th century, and these weapons remained in use until the early 20th century. The first automatic machine gun was invented by Hiram Maxim in 1885. The Maxim gun used the recoil force from the previously fired bullet to load instead of manual loading, greatly increasing the rate of fire, far exceeding the early designs of Nordenfelt and Gatling.

Cuirassiers were cavalry units equipped with armor and firearms, first appearing in Europe in the 15th century. The first cuirassiers emerged when armored cavalry such as heavy cavalry and lancers abandoned their lances and adopted pistols as their primary weapon. Cuirassiers reached their peak during the Napoleonic Wars and appeared on the battlefield for the last time in the early stages of World War I. To this day, cuirassiers still serve as ceremonial units in some countries.
Dragoons originally referred to mounted infantry who possessed both cavalry and infantry skills. However, the meaning of dragoon gradually evolved
column3: in the 18th century, dragoons came to refer to regular light cavalry units and members. In the 17th and early 18th centuries, most European armies established dragoon regiments. During the Napoleonic Wars, dragoons were generally regarded as cavalry, though their equipment was still lighter compared to cuirassiers.

column2: Hussars refer to various types of light cavalry originating from Hungary in the 15th century. Later, light cavalry from Europe and other regions adopted their title and distinctive dress. During the Napoleonic Wars, hussars distinguished themselves as cavalry. As light cavalry riding fast horses, they were used for skirmishing and reconnaissance.

Military aviation refers to the use of aircraft or other flying machines for warfare. Heavier-than-air aircraft were early recognized for their military value. As early as 1909, the U.S. Signal Corps purchased a Wright Model A aircraft, and later in 1911, the Italians used various types of aircraft in the Libyan War for reconnaissance, photographic reconnaissance, and bombing. Military aircraft rapidly diversified into various types during World War I, such as reconnaissance, artillery observation planes, fighters, and bombers.

A torpedo is a self-propelled weapon equipped with an explosive warhead. After being launched from the surface or underwater, the torpedo generally travels through the water toward its target and is designed to detonate at or near the point of contact with the target. Even small ships can use this weapon to deal a fatal blow to large warships.
